findings.body: The method returns "Clients" as if it were a client model ID. AvailableRoleMappingResource passes it to realm.getClientById and dereferences the null result, producing a server error instead of listing roles from all clients.
findings.failure_mode: Global client grants yield an invalid identifier that crashes or corrupts downstream client enumeration.
findings.impact: The method returns "Clients" as if it were a client model ID. AvailableRoleMappingResource passes it to realm.getClientById and dereferences the null result, producing a server error instead of listing roles from all clients.
findings.root_cause: The implementation treats the type-level resource name and individual client-resource names as having the same client-ID semantics.
findings.suggested_fix: Detect the Clients type resource and expand it to the IDs of all applicable realm clients, or return an explicit wildcard that every consumer handles safely.
findings.title: An all-clients grant is returned as the literal resource-type name
findings.trigger: A caller has the requested scope on the Clients type resource and getClientsWithPermission evaluates that all-clients resource.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 140 adds resource.getName() to granted set. For the type-level 'Clients' resource, getName() returns 'Clients' (line 249 shows resource name equals type). AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:230 passes this to realm.getClientById() which returns null for 'Clients' string, causing NPE on getRolesStream().

findings.body: The authorization check throws UnsupportedOperationException, causing the token endpoint to return an internal server error rather than a deterministic denial or a supported V2 authorization result.
findings.evidence: throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2");
findings.failure_mode: A normal token-exchange request escapes the permission layer as an unhandled runtime exception.
findings.impact: The authorization check throws UnsupportedOperationException, causing the token endpoint to return an internal server error rather than a deterministic denial or a supported V2 authorization result.
findings.root_cause: A production authorization callback inherited by the V2 management object is implemented by throwing rather than by returning an authorization decision.
findings.suggested_fix: Return false for unsupported V2 token exchange authorization, or implement a V2 token-exchange scope and evaluation path; add a test for the combined feature configuration.
findings.title: Legacy token exchange now fails with an unsupported-operation server error
findings.trigger: Legacy token exchange is enabled alongside V2 admin permissions and AbstractTokenExchangeProvider checks whether an authorized client may exchange to a target client.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 149 throws UnsupportedOperationException for canExchangeTo. AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:276 calls AdminPermissions.management().clients().canExchangeTo() which would use ClientPermissionsV2 when V2 is enabled. This causes 500 error instead of proper authorization decision when token exchange is attempted with V2 enabled.

raw_findings.body: The existing resource server has no Clients type resource and lacks the newly introduced configure and role-mapping scopes. Client permission creation fails validation, while evaluation can return false or dereference a missing type resource instead of honoring configured permissions.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Persisted V2 authorization data remains on the old schema after upgrade and cannot support the new client authorization paths.
raw_findings.impact: The existing resource server has no Clients type resource and lacks the newly introduced configure and role-mapping scopes. raw_findings.root_cause: The static schema is expanded, but AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns immediately whenever the admin-permissions client already exists and therefore never reconciles persisted schema data.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add an idempotent schema-reconciliation or migration step that creates missing scopes and type resources for existing admin-permissions resource servers, and cover an upgrade from the previous Users-only schema.
raw_findings.title: Existing V2 realms are not migrated to the newly expanded schema
raw_findings.trigger: A realm whose V2 admin-permissions client was initialized before this patch is upgraded and then a client permission is created or evaluated.

raw_findings.body: Both objects resolve to the same unqualified authorization resource name. Shared scopes such as view, manage, and map-roles can consequently cause a user permission to authorize operations on the client or vice versa, while type-specific scopes can fail to attach.

validated_findings.trigger: A realm whose V2 admin-permissions client was initialized before this patch is upgraded and then a client permission is created or evaluated.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that init() returns immediately without reconciling schema is speculative. The patch shows init() returns early if client exists (line 226-227), but this is pre-existing behavior. The patch only expands the static schema definition. No evidence that upgrade migration is missing - this is a design assumption not proven by the patch.

validated_findings.body: Both objects resolve to the same unqualified authorization resource name. Shared scopes such as view, manage, and map-roles can consequently cause a user permission to authorize operations on the client or vice versa, while type-specific scopes can fail to attach.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Distinct administrative objects become represented by one authorization resource, allowing permissions to cross resource-type boundaries.
validated_findings.impact: Both objects resolve to the same unqualified authorization resource name. Shared scopes such as view, manage, and map-roles can consequently cause a user permission to authorize operations on the client or vice versa, while type-specific scopes can fail to attach.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new client branch places client IDs in the same resource-name namespace already used for user IDs, while existing-resource lookup is name-only.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use resource names or attributes qualified by resource type, and require the expected type when resolving an existing resource; include migration handling for already-created resources.
validated_findings.title: Client and user authorization resources can collide on the same model ID
validated_findings.trigger: A realm contains a client and a user with the same internal ID, which can occur when representations with explicit IDs are imported, and permissions are created for both objects.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about namespace collision is speculative. resolveClient returns client.getId() (line 183), and resolveUser returns user.getId() (line 172). These are UUIDs generated by Keycloak which are globally unique across entity types. The trigger scenario of matching IDs between user and client is unrealistic with UUID generation.

validated_findings.body: The individual resource is not found, so evaluation falls back to the all-clients resource and silently ignores the client-specific permission.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Valid per-client grants are evaluated against the wrong resource and are denied or replaced by global authorization behavior.
validated_findings.impact: The individual resource is not found, so evaluation falls back to the all-clients resource and silently ignores the client-specific permission.
validated_findings.root_cause: Creation stores resourceServer.getClientId() as the owner, but the new evaluator filters lookup by server.getId().
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use the same owner value used by AdminPermissionsSchema when creating resources, or use the owner-independent two-argument findByName overload as UserPermissionsV2 does.
validated_findings.title: Individual client lookup uses an owner different from the one used at creation
validated_findings.trigger: An individual client resource was created by AdminPermissionsSchema with owner resourceServer.getClientId(), and the resource server's ID differs from its client ID.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about owner mismatch is incorrect. Line 214 uses findByName with server.getId() as owner, but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource at line 104 creates resources with resourceServer.getClientId() as owner. However, UserPermissionsV2 at line 117 uses findByName without owner parameter. The V2 pattern appears intentional - the claim conflates V1 and V2 patterns.

validated_findings.body: AvailableRoleMappingResource still tests ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ rather than ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2, takes the broad-role branch, and denies the request instead of invoking this V2 permission lookup. The administration UI cannot list roles that the V2 grant should expose.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The newly implemented evaluator is bypassed on the production V2 request path.
validated_findings.impact: AvailableRoleMappingResource still tests ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ rather than ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2, takes the broad-role branch, and denies the request instead of invoking this V2 permission lookup. The administration UI cannot list roles that the V2 grant should expose.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch installs a V2 implementation for getClientsWithPermission without updating its V1-gated consumers.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Update all AvailableRoleMappingResource feature checks to recognize V2 and add endpoint tests using only V2 client mapping permissions.
validated_findings.title: V2 client role-listing permissions remain unreachable behind V1-only feature gates
validated_findings.trigger: An administrator has only a V2 map-roles or map-roles-composite client permission and requests available role mappings through AvailableRoleMappingResource.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that AvailableRoleMappingResource gates on V1 only is not proven by the patch. The patch shows ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission implementation. AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:229 shows it calls auth.clients().getClientsWithPermission() which would use V2 implementation when V2 is enabled via AdminPermissions factory methods.

validated_findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema creates object resources without assigning their resource type, so findByType("Clients") does not visit the per-client resource and the authorized client's roles are omitted.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The permission enumeration returns an empty or incomplete client-ID set despite valid per-client grants.
validated_findings.impact: AdminPermissionsSchema creates object resources without assigning their resource type, so findByType("Clients") does not visit the per-client resource and the authorized client's roles are omitted.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new query assumes every client object resource is tagged with Clients, but the shared schema creation path only sets its name, owner, and scopes.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Set resource.setType(resourceType) when AdminPermissionsSchema creates an object resource, migrate existing object resources, and test this query with an individual client permission.
validated_findings.title: Per-client resources are omitted by the type-filtered permission query
validated_findings.trigger: A caller has a map-roles permission targeting one client and getClientsWithPermission is used to build the set of available client roles.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that object resources lack type is speculative. AdminPermissionsSchema.init() at lines 247-252 creates type-level resources with resource.setType(type). The getOrCreateResource method creates individual resources without explicit type, but findByType queries type-level resources. The design appears intentional for type-level vs individual resource distinction.

validated_findings.body: The method returns "Clients" as if it were a client model ID. AvailableRoleMappingResource passes it to realm.getClientById and dereferences the null result, producing a server error instead of listing roles from all clients.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Global client grants yield an invalid identifier that crashes or corrupts downstream client enumeration.
validated_findings.impact: The method returns "Clients" as if it were a client model ID. AvailableRoleMappingResource passes it to realm.getClientById and dereferences the null result, producing a server error instead of listing roles from all clients.
validated_findings.root_cause: The implementation treats the type-level resource name and individual client-resource names as having the same client-ID semantics.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Detect the Clients type resource and expand it to the IDs of all applicable realm clients, or return an explicit wildcard that every consumer handles safely.
validated_findings.title: An all-clients grant is returned as the literal resource-type name
validated_findings.trigger: A caller has the requested scope on the Clients type resource and getClientsWithPermission evaluates that all-clients resource.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 140 adds resource.getName() to granted set. For the type-level 'Clients' resource, getName() returns 'Clients' (line 249 shows resource name equals type). AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:230 passes this to realm.getClientById() which returns null for 'Clients' string, causing NPE on getRolesStream().

validated_findings.body: The authorization check throws UnsupportedOperationException, causing the token endpoint to return an internal server error rather than a deterministic denial or a supported V2 authorization result.
validated_findings.evidence: throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2");
validated_findings.failure_mode: A normal token-exchange request escapes the permission layer as an unhandled runtime exception.
validated_findings.impact: The authorization check throws UnsupportedOperationException, causing the token endpoint to return an internal server error rather than a deterministic denial or a supported V2 authorization result.
validated_findings.root_cause: A production authorization callback inherited by the V2 management object is implemented by throwing rather than by returning an authorization decision.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Return false for unsupported V2 token exchange authorization, or implement a V2 token-exchange scope and evaluation path; add a test for the combined feature configuration.
validated_findings.title: Legacy token exchange now fails with an unsupported-operation server error
validated_findings.trigger: Legacy token exchange is enabled alongside V2 admin permissions and AbstractTokenExchangeProvider checks whether an authorized client may exchange to a target client.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 149 throws UnsupportedOperationException for canExchangeTo. AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:276 calls AdminPermissions.management().clients().canExchangeTo() which would use ClientPermissionsV2 when V2 is enabled. This causes 500 error instead of proper authorization decision when token exchange is attempted with V2 enabled.

validated_findings.body: The ClientRemovedEvent cleanup is skipped, leaving stale resources and associated policies in the realm's admin-permissions resource server. They remain visible through authorization APIs and can later cause invalid client IDs or stale grants if an ID is restored.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Model deletion and authorization data deletion become inconsistent, accumulating orphaned security state.
validated_findings.impact: The ClientRemovedEvent cleanup is skipped, leaving stale resources and associated policies in the realm's admin-permissions resource server. They remain visible through authorization APIs and can later cause invalid client IDs or stale grants if an ID is restored.
validated_findings.root_cause: The listener is newly gated exclusively on the V1 feature even though this patch starts persisting per-client resources for V2.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Handle client removal for V2 with schema-aware resource and policy deletion, while retaining the V1 cleanup path separately instead of excluding V2 at the outer feature gate.
validated_findings.title: Deleting a client under V2 leaves its authorization resources and policies orphaned
validated_findings.trigger: A client with an individual V2 authorization resource is deleted while only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 77 gates cleanup on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ only. When only V2 is enabled, ClientRemovedEvent at line 89-91 is never reached. V2 creates per-client resources via getOrCreateResource, but cleanup is skipped, leaving orphaned authorization resources.

validated_findings.body: The documentation incorrectly promises a returned boolean and omits that authorization failure is reported by ForbiddenException, obscuring the method's actual API contract.
validated_findings.failure_mode: API consumers receive incorrect guidance about control flow and error handling.
validated_findings.impact: The documentation incorrectly promises a returned boolean and omits that authorization failure is reported by ForbiddenException, obscuring the method's actual API contract.
validated_findings.root_cause: Documentation for a boolean can-method was copied onto a void require-method.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: State that requireView throws ForbiddenException when canView returns false, matching the other require-method documentation.
validated_findings.title: requireView documentation describes a boolean return instead of its exception contract
validated_findings.trigger: An implementer or caller consults the interface documentation for the void requireView method.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 96-97 documents void requireView() as 'Returns true if canView() returns true' which is incorrect - void methods don't return values. The method throws ForbiddenException on failure per the pattern shown in other require methods.

validated_findings.body: The documentation says the method returns true and does not document its ForbiddenException behavior, misrepresenting the interface contract.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Reviewers and API consumers cannot rely on the interface documentation to understand authorization failures.
validated_findings.impact: The documentation says the method returns true and does not document its ForbiddenException behavior, misrepresenting the interface contract.
validated_findings.root_cause: A can-method return description was copied to a void require-method.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Document that the method throws ForbiddenException when canViewClientScopes returns false.
validated_findings.title: requireViewClientScopes documentation describes a nonexistent boolean result
validated_findings.trigger: An implementer or caller consults the documentation for the void requireViewClientScopes method.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 101 has identical documentation defect as candidate 8 - documents void requireViewClientScopes() as returning true. Same root cause of copying can-method documentation to require-method.

validated_findings.body: The suite covers ordinary role mapping and composite mapping but never exercises the third newly added client mapping scope, so incorrect scope names, evaluation, or endpoint wiring can merge undetected.
validated_findings.evidence: createPermission(client, myclient.getId(), clientsType, Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE), onlyMyAdminUserPolicy);
validated_findings.failure_mode: CI provides no behavioral verification for one complete authorization branch introduced by the patch.
validated_findings.impact: The suite covers ordinary role mapping and composite mapping but never exercises the third newly added client mapping scope, so incorrect scope names, evaluation, or endpoint wiring can merge undetected.
validated_findings.root_cause: The test added for the neighboring mapping scopes omits the newly introduced map-roles-client-scope capability.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a V2 integration test that first denies and then permits an operation guarded by canMapClientScopeRoles using only MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE.
validated_findings.title: The new map-roles-client-scope authorization path has no integration coverage
validated_findings.trigger: The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE schema entry or canMapClientScopeRoles implementation regresses while the client authorization test suite runs.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about missing MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE test coverage is a test gap observation, not a defect in the code. Line 359 shows the test includes CONFIGURE scope. Test coverage gaps are not code defects - the implementation may still be correct.
